name: Fesoterodine pivotal trials
question: Do fixed doses of fesoterodine improve overactive bladder symptoms compared with placebo?

design.population: Adults with increased micturition frequency and urgency, with or without urgency urinary incontinence.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 1205–1207; Results, p 1207; Table 2, p 1208

verdictNote: Both doses met the prespecified micturition, UUI, and treatment-response comparisons versus placebo.
takeaway: In SP583, fesoterodine 4 mg and 8 mg once daily improved micturition frequency, urgency urinary incontinence, and patient-rated treatment response versus placebo at 12 weeks. The 8 mg arm had one catheterization for acute urinary retention.

reports.label: International pivotal trial (SP583)
reports.citation: Chapple C, Van Kerrebroeck P, Tubaro A, et al. "Clinical efficacy, safety, and tolerability of once-daily fesoterodine in subjects with overactive bladder." *Eur Urol.* 2007;52(4):1204-1212. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2007.07.009

results.measure: Least-squares mean change from baseline to week 12 in the full analysis set, with last observation carried forward
results.note: P<0.001 for each fesoterodine dose versus placebo; tolterodine P=0.001. No between-group confidence intervals reported.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3, p 1209; Statistical analyses, p 1207

results.endpoint: Urgency urinary incontinence episodes per 24 hours
results.measure: Least-squares mean change from baseline to week 12 among participants with at least one baseline urgency incontinence episode; last observation carried forward
results.note: P=0.001 for 4 mg and P<0.001 for 8 mg versus placebo; tolterodine P=0.008. No between-group confidence intervals reported.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3 and footnote §, p 1209

results.measure: Yes response at week 12: greatly improved or improved on the four-point treatment benefit scale, in the full analysis set
results.note: P<0.001 for each active treatment versus placebo. Response numerators and between-group confidence intervals were not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Table 1, p 1206; Table 3, p 1209

results.measure: Least-squares mean change in mL from baseline to week 12; last observation carried forward
results.note: Exploratory secondary-endpoint comparisons versus placebo: P<0.001 for each fesoterodine dose; tolterodine P=0.002. No between-group confidence intervals reported.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3 and footnote, p 1209

results.measure: Least-squares mean change from baseline to week 12; last observation carried forward
results.note: Exploratory secondary-endpoint comparisons versus placebo: P=0.394 for 4 mg, P=0.418 for 8 mg, and P=0.336 for tolterodine; none reached nominal significance.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3 and footnote, p 1209

harms.label: Dry mouth, constipation, and any treatment-emergent adverse event
harms.note: Safety population; treatment-emergent events irrespective of attribution.

harms.label: Urinary retention and catheterization

values.feso8: urinary retention 2/287; discontinuation for retention 0/287; acute urinary retention requiring catheterization 1/287

harms.locator: Full text, Safety and tolerability, p 1210; corrigendum, Eur Urol 2009;56:236
harms.note: The 2009 corrigendum replaces the original statement that no acute urinary retention required catheterization; the catheterized participant was male and assigned fesoterodine 8 mg. Only the 4 mg retention event led to discontinuation.

harms.label: Adverse-event discontinuation
harms.locator: Full text, Safety and tolerability, pp 1210–1211
harms.note: Discontinued the trial prematurely because of an adverse event; 36/1132 overall.

delivery.label: Fixed-dose treatment
delivery.value: After a 2-week placebo run-in, participants received fesoterodine 4 mg or 8 mg, tolterodine ER 4 mg, or placebo once each morning for 12 weeks in a double-blind, double-dummy design at 150 sites in 19 countries. Eligibility required age at least 18 years, at least 6 months of urgency symptoms, at least 8 micturitions per 24 hours, and either at least 6 urgency or at least 3 UUI episodes in a 3-day baseline diary; baseline PVR greater than 100 mL and clinically relevant outlet obstruction were excluded. Efficacy used a full analysis set (randomized, treated, and with baseline and double-blind micturition data); safety included all treated participants (1132/1135).
delivery.locator: Full text, Study design and Subjects, pp 1205–1206; corrigendum, Eur Urol 2008;53:1319; Statistical analyses and Results, p 1207

reports.label: Separate US pivotal trial (SP584)
reports.citation: Nitti VW, Dmochowski R, Sand PK, et al. "Efficacy, safety and tolerability of fesoterodine for overactive bladder syndrome." *J Urol.* 2007;178(6):2488-2494. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2007.08.033

results.measure: Least-squares mean change from baseline to study end; 800 analyzed with last observation carried forward
results.note: P=0.032 for 4 mg and P<0.001 for 8 mg versus placebo; least-squares mean change, with no contrast confidence intervals reported.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 2491; Statistical Analysis, p 2490

results.endpoint: Urgency urinary incontinence episodes per 24 hours
results.measure: Least-squares mean change from baseline to study end among participants incontinent at baseline
results.note: P=0.003 for 4 mg and P<0.001 for 8 mg versus placebo; 651 participants had at least one baseline urgency incontinence episode.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and footnote, p 2491

results.note: Yes meant improved or greatly improved on the four-point Treatment Benefit scale; P<0.001 for each fesoterodine dose versus placebo. Response numerators were not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 2491; Appendix, p 2493

results.measure: Least-squares mean change in mL from baseline to study end
results.note: Nominal comparisons versus placebo: P=0.150 for 4 mg and P<0.001 for 8 mg; secondary endpoints were outside the multiplicity-controlled primary testing sequence.

harms.label: Dry mouth, constipation, and urinary tract infection

values.feso4: dry mouth 45/282; constipation 14/282; urinary tract infection 10/282
values.feso8: dry mouth 99/279; constipation 21/279; urinary tract infection 15/279
values.placebo: dry mouth 19/271; constipation 7/271; urinary tract infection 11/271

harms.note: Treatment-emergent events in the safety population; urinary tract infection was 10/282 with 4 mg versus 11/271 with placebo.

harms.label: Urinary retention and increased post-void residual

values.feso4: urinary retention AE 4/282; post-void residual >200 mL in 1/282
values.feso8: urinary retention AE 6/279; post-void residual >200 mL in 7/279
values.placebo: urinary retention AE 1/271; post-void residual >200 mL in 0/271

harms.locator: Full text, Tolerability and Safety, pp 2491-2492; Table 3, p 2492
harms.note: Eight participants had post-void residual >200 mL; none required catheterization. Urinary retention and increased residual could overlap.

harms.label: Adverse-event withdrawal
harms.note: Dry mouth led to withdrawal in 3/282 and 5/279 fesoterodine recipients; urinary retention or increased residual led to withdrawal in 2/282 and 3/279.

harms.label: Any treatment-emergent adverse event
harms.note: All treatment-emergent adverse events, irrespective of attribution to study medication.

delivery.label: US trial treatment and eligibility
delivery.value: Fesoterodine 4 mg (283 randomized), fesoterodine 8 mg (279), or placebo (274) once daily for 12 weeks; 836 total randomized. Overactive bladder duration was at least six months; neurogenic overactive bladder, clinically relevant obstruction, and baseline post-void residual >100 mL were excluded.
delivery.locator: Full text, Abstract, p 2488; Subject Selection and Study Design, p 2489

delivery.label: Study medication adherence and completion
delivery.value: At least 96% were compliant with study medication during the double-blind phase; 681/836 randomized participants completed 12 weeks.
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, Subjects, p 2490; Discontinuations, p 2492

reports.label: Pooled open-label extensions
reports.citation: Scarpero H, Sand PK, Kelleher CJ, et al. "Long-term safety, tolerability, and efficacy of fesoterodine treatment in men and women with overactive bladder symptoms." *Curr Med Res Opin.* 2011;27(5):921-930. doi:10.1185/03007995.2011.559581
reports.followUp: Open-label treatment assessed through 24 months; maximum allowed 24-36 months
reports.followUpLocator: PubMed abstract, Research Design and Methods and Main Outcome Measures

results.measure: Change from double-blind baseline through open-label month 24
results.note: In pooled flexible-dose extension participants followed through month 24, improvements were sustained or further improved. Open-label extensions pooled participants from SP583 and SP584; all began at 8 mg, with dose reduction and re-escalation permitted.
results.locator: Scarpero PubMed abstract, Research Design and Methods and Results

harms.label: Dry mouth in pooled flexible-dose extension
harms.note: All participants began at 8 mg; annual dose reduction to 4 mg and re-escalation were permitted. Rates are by sex, not randomized dose.

delivery.label: Continuation through 24 months
delivery.value: 83/185 men (45%) and 356/705 women (50%) continued open-label fesoterodine for at least 24 months.
